title: The Shortest Subarray From Each Start That Reaches the Largest OR

concept.title: The largest OR from a start is the OR of the whole suffix; the shortest subarray must reach the nearest occurrence of every bit
body: For every starting position `i` consider the subarrays that **start at `i`**. Their ORs grow when the subarray gets longer, so the **largest OR** is the OR of the whole suffix `a[i..n-1]`. Print, for every `i`, the **length of the shortest subarray starting at `i` whose OR equals this largest OR**. For `1 0 2 1 3` the answers are `3 3 2 2 1`: from the position 0 the suffix OR is 3 and `1 0 2` already reaches it.

For a bit `b`, the subarray must contain **a number with this bit** if the suffix has it at all; the shortest way is to reach the **nearest** number at or after `i` that has the bit `b`. So the answer for `i` is the farthest of these nearest positions over all bits that occur in the suffix, plus one, minus `i` (and at least 1). Scan the array from the right to the left, keeping `last[b]`, the nearest position at or to the right of the current one that has the bit `b` (or -1).

The loop makes 30 steps for each of the `n` positions, so the program runs in O(30 n). The idea that the OR is built bit by bit is the same as the one in the "shortest window with all letters" problems: every needed element has to be inside, so the window ends at the farthest of the nearest ones. The OR of the subarray `i..far` contains every bit of the suffix, hence equals the suffix OR, and no shorter subarray can contain all these bits.

statement: A list of `n` numbers is given. For every starting position `i` print the length of the shortest subarray that starts at `i` and whose bitwise OR is equal to the largest OR of all subarrays that start at `i` (that is, the OR of `a[i..n-1]`).
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of values.
outputFormat: Print `n` numbers on one line, separated by spaces.

examples.note: The suffix ORs are 3, 3, 3, 3, 3; the shortest subarrays are 1 0 2 (3), 0 2 1 (3), 2 1 (2), 1 3 (2) and 3 (1): 3 3 2 2 1.

hints: The largest OR from a start is the OR of the entire suffix.
Every bit of the suffix must be reached at its nearest occurrence.
Scan from the right and keep, for each bit, the nearest position that has it.

explanation: Scanning from the right, for every bit the nearest position at or after the current one that has it is kept; the shortest subarray from the current start ends at the farthest of these nearest positions (or at the start itself).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

last = [-1] * 30
res = [0] * n
for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
    far = i
    x = a[i]
    for b in range(30):
        if (x >> b) & 1:
            last[b] = i
        if last[b] > far:
            far = last[b]
    res[i] = far - i + 1
print(*res)
